names.name: COLORS
names.summary: Names for the named colours: ``f.COLORS.TOMATO`` is the word ``"tomato"``.

names.name: CONSTANTS
names.summary: Names for the words that choose an option, in groups, so an editor can list them and a typing slip is caught.

members.name: LEFT
members.meaning: x is where the text starts; it runs to the right. The default.

members.name: CENTER
members.meaning: Across: x is the middle of the text. Up and down: y is halfway between the top and the bottom.

members.name: RIGHT
members.meaning: x is where the text ends.

members.name: JUSTIFY
members.meaning: In text_box(), each line is stretched to the box's width by widening the spaces, except the last line of a paragraph and a line of one word. In text() the same as left.

members.name: TOP
members.meaning: y is the top of the text: the tallest letters' height (the font's ascent). The default.

members.name: BASELINE
members.meaning: y is the line the letters stand on; the tails of g, p and y hang below it. Lines of text in different sizes line up on their baselines.

members.name: BOTTOM
members.meaning: y is the bottom of the text: below the tails of g, p and y (the font's descent).

members.name: NORMAL
members.meaning: Upright letters of the usual weight. The default.

members.name: BOLD
members.meaning: Thicker, heavier letters, for emphasis and headlines.

members.name: ITALIC
members.meaning: Letters slanted to the right (the built-in font's oblique).

members.name: BOLD_ITALIC
members.meaning: Bold and slanted.

members.name: ROUND
members.meaning: Each end of a line is a half circle, so the line reaches half its width past its end points. The default.

members.name: SQUARE
members.meaning: Each end is squared off half the line's width past its end point.

members.name: BUTT
members.meaning: Each end is cut off flat exactly at its end point.

members.name: ROUND
members.meaning: Corners are rounded. The default.

members.name: MITER
members.meaning: Corners come to a sharp point. A very sharp corner is cut flat instead, so the point does not shoot far out.

members.name: BEVEL
members.meaning: Corners are cut off flat.

members.name: ARROW
members.meaning: The usual pointer. The default.

members.name: CROSS
members.meaning: A thin cross, for aiming at a point.

members.name: HAND
members.meaning: A pointing hand, as over a link: something can be clicked.

members.name: MOVE
members.meaning: Four arrows: something can be dragged.

members.name: TEXT
members.meaning: The I-beam: text can be typed or selected.

members.name: WAIT
members.meaning: The busy pointer (an hourglass or a spinning circle).

members.name: NORMAL
members.meaning: The new colour covers the old one (see-through only as far as its alpha or opacity() says).

members.name: MULTIPLY
members.meaning: Multiplies the colours, so the result is always darker: like overlapping inks or colour filters. White leaves the old colour unchanged; black gives black.

members.name: SCREEN
members.meaning: The opposite of multiply: the result is always lighter, like two slide projectors on one screen. Black leaves the old colour unchanged; white gives white.

members.name: OVERLAY
members.meaning: Multiply where the old colour is dark, screen where it is light: more contrast, keeping the old picture's highlights and shadows.

members.name: DARKEN
members.meaning: Keeps the darker of the two colours, channel by channel (red, green and blue separately).

members.name: LIGHTEN
members.meaning: Keeps the lighter of the two colours, channel by channel.

members.name: ADD
members.meaning: Adds the colours, so overlaps glow and turn white quickly: light added to light.

members.name: DIFFERENCE
members.meaning: The difference between the colours: the same colours give black, white turns the old colour into its opposite (a negative).

members.name: EXCLUSION
members.meaning: Like difference, with less contrast: white still inverts, mid-grey gives grey.

members.name: DODGE
members.meaning: Brightens the old colour by the new one; bright new colours burn out to white (color dodge). Black changes nothing.

members.name: BURN
members.meaning: Darkens the old colour by the new one, with more contrast (color burn). White changes nothing.

members.name: HARD_LIGHT
members.meaning: Multiply where the new colour is dark, screen where it is light: like a harsh spotlight of the new colour.

members.name: SOFT_LIGHT
members.meaning: A gentler hard_light: like a soft, diffused light of the new colour. Mid-grey changes nothing.

members.name: HUE
members.meaning: The new colour's hue with the old colour's saturation and lightness: recolours the old picture.

members.name: SATURATION
members.meaning: The new colour's saturation with the old colour's hue and lightness: makes the old picture more vivid or greyer.

members.name: COLOR
members.meaning: The new colour's hue and saturation with the old colour's lightness: tints the old picture while keeping its shading.

members.name: LUMINOSITY
members.meaning: The new colour's lightness with the old colour's hue and saturation: the opposite of color.

members.name: THRESHOLD
members.meaning: Every pixel becomes black or white: white where its brightness is above the value (0 to 1, default 0.5).

members.name: GRAY
members.meaning: Every pixel becomes the grey of its brightness: a black-and-white picture.

members.name: OPAQUE
members.meaning: Makes every pixel fully opaque, removing any see-through parts.

members.name: INVERT
members.meaning: Every colour becomes its opposite, like a photographic negative: black and white swap, red becomes cyan.

members.name: BLUR
members.meaning: Softens the picture; the value is the radius in pixels (default 1). Larger is blurrier.

members.name: POSTERIZE
members.meaning: Each colour channel keeps only that many levels (2 to 255, required), giving flat bands of colour like a screen print.

members.name: ERODE
members.meaning: Each pixel takes the darkest colour around it: dark shapes grow, light ones shrink and thin lines of light vanish.

members.name: DILATE
members.meaning: Each pixel takes the lightest colour around it: light shapes grow, dark ones shrink.

members.name: SINE
members.meaning: A pure, smooth tone with no overtones, like a tuning fork or a whistle.

members.name: SQUARE
members.meaning: Hollow and buzzy, like an old video game or a clarinet's low notes.

members.name: SAW
members.meaning: Bright and brassy, the richest in overtones: a classic synthesiser sound.

members.name: TRIANGLE
members.meaning: Between sine and square: soft but a little reedy, like a flute.

members.name: SOFT
members.meaning: A sine with a few gentle overtones: warm and round, good for melodies.

members.name: NOISE
members.meaning: Random hiss with no pitch, like wind, the sea or a drum's snare. The frequency is ignored.

members.name: ORIGIN
members.meaning: The mark's own (0, 0): the point it was drawn around. The default.

members.name: CENTER
members.meaning: The middle of the mark's bounds().

members.name: TOP
members.meaning: The middle of the top edge.

members.name: BOTTOM
members.meaning: The middle of the bottom edge.

members.name: LEFT
members.meaning: The middle of the left edge.

members.name: RIGHT
members.meaning: The middle of the right edge.

members.name: TOP_LEFT
members.meaning: The top-left corner of the bounds.

members.name: TOP_RIGHT
members.meaning: The top-right corner.

members.name: BOTTOM_LEFT
members.meaning: The bottom-left corner.

members.name: BOTTOM_RIGHT
members.meaning: The bottom-right corner.

members.name: DOWN
